articles.title: A former California oil field has faced development pressure for 50 years; after a 25-year preservation fight, supporters are $20 million short of a $95 million land purchase
articles.summary: US News: For 50 years, West Coyote Hills in Fullerton, California, has faced the threat of development. The 510-acre open space is a former oil field owned by .
articles.body: For 50 years, West Coyote Hills in Fullerton, California, has faced the threat of development. The 510-acre open space is a former oil field owned by Chevron-Pacific Coast Homes and surrounded by parts three cities- La Mirada, Buena Park and La Habra.Now, after 25 years of community efforts to preserve the land, the campaign to protect the remaining portion has entered its final stage. Friends of Coyote Hills says more than 75% of the funding needed to buy the property has been secured, but $20 million is still required to complete the $95 million purchase.The conservation group is seeking the remaining funding to permanently protect the west side of Coyote Hills as parkland and a nature preserve. If the purchase is completed, the total protected area will reach 582 acres, including the Robert E Ward Nature Preserve.The effort began in 2001, when a small group of local residents came together to protect one of the last large natural open spaces in the North Orange County–South Los Angeles region. Over the next 25 years, their campaign has led to the protection of more than 200 acres on the eastern side of the site.A long fight The first major breakthrough came in 2014, when advocacy efforts resulted in a density shift that protected about 121 acres.In December 2021, the City of Fullerton acquired about 24 acres next to what later became the Robert E Ward Nature Preserve. The purchase, supported by significant funding from the State of California and private funders, expanded the preserve to about 72 acres.The community was then able to experience part of the protected land directly. In 2023, more than two miles of recreational trails opened at the Robert E Ward Nature Preserve. According to Friends of Coyote Hills, this allowed the public to experience the natural area for the first time in nearly 50 years.The next major step came in April 2026 when the State of California approved the Purchase and Sale Agreement, authorising the Watershed Conservation Authority to buy the remaining site from Chevron-Pacific Coast Homes for $95 million.Of that amount, $75 million has already been committed. The remaining $20 million is the final funding gap before the acquisition can be completed.Habitat for threatened speciesWest Coyote Hills contains coastal sage scrub habitat and supports a range of wildlife and plant species.Friends of Coyote Hills says the property supports 56 pairs of threatened California gnatcatchers, described by the group as the largest population in Southern California. It also supports 69 pairs of coastal cactus wrens, which are listed as a California State Species of Special Concern.The Fullerton Observer reported that West Coyote Hills supports 368 additional species. These include the endangered least Bell’s vireo, tricoloured blackbird, white-tailed kite, intermediate mariposa lily and coastal cactus wren.The conservation group describes the site as part of a biodiversity hotspot and says the area is home to 15 rare, endangered and sensitive species.Protecting the remaining land would also preserve one of the largest unpaved portions of the Lower San Gabriel River Watershed. It could also help downstream coastal and marine resources by avoiding water quality impacts linked to increased urban stormwater runoff.Push for $20 million gapThe planned Phase 2 acquisition is expected to close between 2026 and 2027, according to the organisation. Completing it would permanently protect the remaining habitat and bring the total protected acreage to 582 acres.Friends of Coyote Hills says the campaign has been working towards this goal for 25 years. The group says its mission is to save all 510 acres of West Coyote Hills as a park and nature preserve for present and future generations.More than one million people live within a seven-mile radius of West Coyote Hills, while the wider area served by the site includes more than two million residents in park-poor communities across Orange and Los Angeles counties.The property has several potential public uses, including habitat protection, restoration, trails, bikeways, scenic access and education. West Coyote Hills is an outdoor educational resource because of its ecology and archaeological history.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said Friday India is exploring ideas with both Russia and Ukraine to bring the conflict to an end, while again defending India's energy sourcing and underlining that it's important to "diagnose" the problem right. The minister had said in Ukraine a day ago that the conflict will end through dialogue and diplomacy and not oil trade.Without revealing if there was any specific peace proposal under consideration, Jaishankar said India was having "detailed discussions" with both sides about possible ways to facilitate peace. He was speaking in Warsaw after a meeting with his Polish counterpart Radoslaw Sikorski."PM Modi and President Putin met in Bishkek three days ago, and then I went to Kyiv. So, what we had were discussions with the Russian side, yesterday with the Ukrainian side, and what we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they would contribute to the mitigation, ideally the cessation of the conflict," he said.India has so far not come up with a plan of its own to ensure a ceasefire as it believes the primary responsibility to end the war lies with Russia and Ukraine. However, as Jaishankar reiterated, it's ready to offer any assistance, if required, to ensure peace.After Modi's renewed peace message to Putin, there seems to be more urgency in India's efforts, with Jaishankar calling on Zelensky and discussing "approaches to end the ongoing conflict"." ...We must each do what we can, in whichever way we believe would be most effective. And support the efforts of others to bring this conflict to an end. This is India's strong conviction, and we are acting on it," Jaishankar said in Poland. "I think let's diagnose the problem right. The issue is a conflict, and the solution to that is not in trade. The solution... is in negotiations."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has directed National Testing Agency (NTA) to declare within 24 hours the NEET-UG re-examination results of two candidates, whose results were withheld over allegations linking them to the question paper leak. Justice Jasmeet Singh pointed out the candidates had not been named as accused by CBI in its chargesheet.While CBI told the court that it did not make them accused, though they had paid money to get question papers, the judge observed that at this stage, it was just an allegation and "therefore, the petitioners cannot be treated as persons against whom criminal culpability has been established or as having been found guilty of any illegality".The court was hearing the students' plea seeking release of their re-NEET results and permission to participate in the ongoing counselling. The CBI chargesheet named the two petitioners as witnesses, and not accused. NTA, however, issued show-cause notices to them and withheld their results.During the hearing, NTA submitted that it withheld the results after CBI informed it that several candidates had allegedly received or shared the question paper of the May 3 examination.On its part, CBI submitted that the petitioners had received the question paper and had the "mens rea" (intent) to commit the illegality, since money had been paid by them for obtaining the question paper.HC observed that the petitioners were at a "nascent stage of their academic careers", and withholding their results merely on the basis of allegations that were yet to be tested would cause serious prejudice to them."The petitioners ought to be permitted to know their results and, subject to the outcome of the proceedings, participate in the further rounds of counseling conducted by the NTA," Justice Singh said. The order recorded denying them an opportunity to participate in counselling at this stage could result in consequences that may not subsequently be adequately remedied.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has rewarded a wrongdoer - a man who got appointed as a junior civil engineer in Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) by producing a forged ST certificate, and, subsequently, stalled the scrutiny of his eligibility for quota for more than a decade - by allowing him to superannuate in peace with retirement benefits.Shirish P Patil got a certificate in 1984 by identifying himself as belonging to the 'Tokre Koli' Scheduled Tribe community. Based on the certificate, he was appointed a junior civil engineer in MCGM in 1994. He misplaced the original ST certificate but managed to secure a fresh one from the sub-divisional magistrate, Bhusawal division, in Oct 2000.Following scrutiny initiated by MCGM, the Police Vigilance Cell traced Patil's family history and found that his ancestors had been recorded as 'Koli', 'Hindu Koli' and 'Hindu Suryawanshi Koli', none of which belonged to the ST category. In July 2009, MCGM issued a show cause notice to Patil.He successfully dodged and delayed proceedings before the scrutiny committee until Jan 2020, when the panel rejected his plea that his lawyer and elderly family members were not available, and invalidated the ST certificate. HC dismissed his appeal against cancellation of ST status.SC, however, stayed Patil's dismissal from service through an interim order on Nov 18, 2021. As a result, the engineer continued to serve until June 30, 2025, when he retired after being employed with MCGM for more than three decades based on a forged ST certificate.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi Thursday upheld the cancellation of Patil's ST certificate and Bombay HC order. However, it took a lenient view given his undertaking that he or any of his family members "shall (not) be entitled to claim any future benefit on the basis of the invalidated ST certificate".The ruling contrasts with SC's consistent rulings against benefits accruing to people who forge SC or ST certificates to gain admission or employment.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Ohio State pays $2.1M settlement as it admits researcher had ‘inappropriate foreign affiliations’ to China
articles.summary: Ohio State University paid $2.1 million to resolve allegations it failed to disclose researcher C.K. Shum's ties to China's Thousand Talents Program.
articles.body: The Ohio State University acknowledged that a former researcher had "inappropriate foreign affiliations" after agreeing to pay $2.1 million to resolve federal allegations that the university failed to share researchers’ ties to China while seeking and receiving taxpayer-funded research grants. The Justice Department alleged Ohio State failed to properly disclose affiliations and financial support involving Chinese universities and state-run research organizations in applications and reports submitted to NASA and the National Science Foundation from 2012-2023. The allegations included a principal investigator’s participation in China’s Thousand Talents Program. Ohio State told Fox News Digital in a statement Friday that the university ultimately uncovered and investigated C.K. Shum’s foreign affiliations itself and reported them to federal authorities. Shum is no longer employed at the university. HARVARD-CHINA LINKS UNEARTHED AS CONGRESS FINDS 140 PAPERS CO-AUTHORED BY CCP MILITARY UNIVERSITIES "Ohio State uncovered and investigated C.K. Shum’s inappropriate foreign affiliations and self-reported them to NASA and the National Science Foundation," Benjamin Johnson, chief communications officer at The Ohio State University, told Fox News Digital in a statement on Friday. "The university suspended Shum’s principal investigator privileges, halted spending on the relevant federal awards, initiated disciplinary proceedings, and repaid the federal grant funds in question. Shum is no longer employed at Ohio State, and the university has cooperated with federal authorities throughout the investigation." Johnson added, "Ohio State takes national security seriously, and the university has long been recognized for its efforts to promote research integrity and security. Safeguards include dedicated research compliance and secure research offices, mandatory conflict-of-interest and research security disclosure systems, and robust security and foreign influence training programs." HARVARD TOPS NATION IN FOREIGN CASH HAUL AS COTTON DEMANDS PROBE INTO CHINA FUNDING In a press release, the Department of Justice said that the grant applications required OSU to share any ties to any foreign government. "The settlement resolves allegations that OSU failed to disclose the collaboration and affiliation with, or funding received from, the PRC by certain OSU employees working on NASA and NSF grants," the press release read. "Specifically, the settlement resolves allegations that since 2014, annual Faculty Activity Reports submitted to OSU identified affiliations with PRC universities and state-run research organizations, but OSU did not disclose this information to NASA or NSF." The press release also noted that Ohio State became aware in 2019 that a researcher tied to NASA-funded work was involved in China’s Thousand Talents Program, but waited until 2023 to inform NASA and the National Science Foundation. The federal government describes the program as a Beijing-backed effort to attract people with expertise in or access to overseas technology and intellectual property. The DOJ also said they also found other OSU employees connected to the grants who had relationships with Chinese entities or received Chinese funding. "We will continue to hold accountable any university that fails to comply with disclosure requirements designed to protect research security and federally-funded scientific achievements." articles.title: Zelenskyy proposes ceasefire with Russia ahead of US envoys’ Kyiv visit
articles.summary: Europe News: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has proposed a ceasefire with Russia as US envoys visit Moscow and Kyiv, saying he hopes to host the American .
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has proposed a ceasefire with Russia as US envoys visit Moscow and Kyiv, saying he hopes to host the American officials in Kyiv in the “coming days”.This comes as a Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU security service on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, accusing Moscow of directly targeting the personal office of the SBU chief.The daytime strike came two days before US President Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff and his son-in-law Jared Kushner were expected to visit Kyiv for the first time, a senior Ukrainian official told AFP.Zelenskyy said he had instructed the SBU to deliver an "appropriate, tangible response" to the strike, while Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga described it as a "major escalation"."Unfortunately, a Russian drone hit the central building of the SBU on Volodymyrska Street in Kyiv, opposite the St. Sophia Cathedral," Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram.Russia has intensified its daytime strikes on Ukraine in recent weeks, at times using jet-powered drones that are more difficult for air defences to intercept.However, attacks on government buildings in central Kyiv, which are heavily fortified and surrounded by security barricades, remain rare.Witkoff and Kushner were due to visit Kyiv for the first time, a Ukrainian official told AFP.US-led diplomatic efforts to end Russia’s four-and-a-half-year invasion have stalled in recent months, as Washington has shifted its focus towards the war with Iran.The conflict has become Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II, killing thousands of civilians and hundreds of thousands of troops.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
